bugs.summary: setMethod(<implicit>) can duplicate message from setGeneric
bugs.creator: jaganmn2

comments.creator: jaganmn2
comments.text:
This bug is visible in the installation output of **Matrix**, but we can reproduce it more easily like so:

```
> args(rcond)
function (x, norm = c("O", "I", "1"), triangular = FALSE, uplo = "U", 
    ...) 
NULL
> args(methods:::.implicitTable[["rcond"]])
function (x, norm, ...) 
NULL
> setClass("zzz")
> setMethod("rcond", c(x = "zzz", norm = "missing"), function(x, norm, ...) NULL)
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from 'base' in the global environment
    (from the saved implicit definition)
Creating a generic function for 'rcond' from package 'base' in the global environment
>
```

The first message is from `setGeneric` (called by `setMethod`).  The second message is from `setMethod` itself.  The latter is clearly redundant.

The first message is not signaled for all implicit generic functions.  It is signaled only those whose signature differs (modulo the existence of `"..."`) from the original function, as determined by a call to `methods:::.identicalGeneric` inside of `setGeneric`.  Hence, for `colSums`, there is no duplication:

```
> args(colSums)
function (x, na.rm = FALSE, dims = 1L) 
NULL
> args(methods:::.implicitTable[["colSums"]])
function (x, na.rm = FALSE, dims = 1, ...) 
NULL
> setClass("zzz")
> setMethod("colSums", c(x = "zzz"), function(x, na.rm = FALSE, dims = 1, ...) NULL)
Creating a generic function for 'colSums' from package 'base' in the global environment
>
```

(Actually, whether `"..."` is ignored depends on the third argument of `methods:::.identicalGeneric`.  `setGeneric` passes `!nzchar(Sys.getenv("R_SETGENERIC_PICKY_DOTS"))` which is typically `TRUE`.)

I can think of two ways to avoid duplication:

* Have `setGeneric` signal a message with a special class.  Then have `setMethod` catch messages of that class, in order to know whether its own message would be redundant.

* Have `setGeneric` gain a `verbose` argument with options like `0=never`, `1=only for non-identical implicit`, `2=also for identical implicit`, `3=always`.  Then have `setMethod` call `setGeneric` with a suitable value for `verbose`.  Then `setMethod` would not need to signal its own message.

Neither is particularly trivial, so I'll wait for comments before devising a patch.

I didn't notice that `formals(colSums)$dims` is `1L`, whereas `formals(methods:::.implicitTable[["colSums"]])` is `1` (i.e., of type `"double"` rather than `"integer"`).  The signatures of `colSums` and `methods:::.implicitTable[["colSums"]]` differ beyond the existence of `"..."`, yet `methods:::.identicalGeneric` reports that they are identical.  That suggests to me that there are other bugs here.  I'll report them separately ...
